correctness.rationale: For each return time k, conditioning on S_k=0 replaces the terminal position by an independent centered future sum of n-k increments, whose expected squared norm is (n-k) tau. Subtracting the unconditional n tau gives the exact local covariance -k tau P(S_k=0), and summation proves the general theorem. For simple walk, the central-binomial return probabilities, two finite binomial identities, a convolution calculation for local-time variance, and the fourth endpoint moment give the displayed closed form and correlation. The packaged checker independently enumerates all simple-walk paths through length 18 and a nonsymmetric centered three-point walk, and replays the symbolic identities exactly.

Statement-level searches for local-time/terminal-energy covariance and return-probability formulations produced no equivalent theorem. A previously derived zero-local-time result couples local time to positive occupation time; it does not imply the endpoint-energy identity because the proof here uses a distinct conditional second-moment argument. A previously derived maximum-endpoint path-symmetry theorem concerns extrema and odd endpoint transforms, not return local time or even quadratic terminal energy.

value.rationale: Origin local time and terminal displacement are canonical observables of a random walk, but their dependence is not visible from either marginal theory. The theorem gives a distribution-free finite identity for every centered iid increment law, resolves the sign into an age-weighted return profile, and in the classical simple walk yields a nonzero limiting correlation with an explicit constant. This is a structural dependence law rather than a finite table or a one-parameter numerical coincidence.
